item.title: Australia's under-16 social media ban faces enforcement challenges
item.description: Australia placed restrictions on social media for under-16s. But the government says Big Tech is dragging its feet on compliance — and many teens are still on the platforms.

item.title: 60 Minutes Transcript: Australia's under-16 social media ban
item.description: Australia, concerned over social media's impact on kids, placed restrictions for children under 16 on many major platforms. It's too soon to say if the law's working, but it's now a global test case.

item.title: The lengths Trump went to for Tina Peters after her sentencing
item.description: President Trump went to extraordinary lengths for Tina Peters, a former election official convicted of helping to breach the very voting system she swore to protect.

item.title: 60 Minutes transcript: Trump, Tina Peters and funds for Colorado
item.description: Tina Peters, an election conspiracy theorist who supported President Trump's voting fraud claims, had her Colorado prison sentence commuted by Gov. Jared Polis after a White House pressure campaign.

item.title: Texas dad deported to Ghana was then forced to go to Mali, he says
item.description: A Texas dad was deported to Ghana, where he says local officials forced him onto a flight to Mali. The problem? A U.S. judge had ruled he couldn't be sent to Mali because the country is unsafe for him.

item.title: Coming up on 60 Minutes: Victor Wembanyama
item.description: The NBA season began and basketball stars are looming large — some of them more than others, like Victor Wembanyama, the 7-foot-4-inch forward-center for the San Antonio Spurs. Jon Wertheim reports next Sunday.

item.title: 60 Minutes Transcript: Inside Trump's third-country deportations
item.description: When immigrants can't be deported to their home countries, the U.S. sometimes sends them to other countries. But some deportees end up in places where U.S. judges have ruled they will likely be persecuted.

item.description: Brazilians are choosing between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro in a polarizing presidential election.

item.title: Vucic concedes defeat in Serbia's parliamentary election
item.description: Aleksandar Vucic, who denounced the oppositional student movement as a foreign-led attempt to unseat him, led with virtually absolute power for 14 years.

item.title: At least 12 injured, including 6 children, in shooting near Florida A&M
item.description: The shooting happened hours after Florida A&M University's homecoming game in Tallahassee.

item.title: Trump says he's weighing deal with Iran against action to "finish them off"
item.description: President Trump said he's deciding between reaching an agreement with Tehran and taking action to "finish them off."

item.title: Four Corners region faces more flood threats following days of heavy rain
item.description: The National Weather Service has issued a flood watch for much of the Four Corners — the meeting point of Arizona, Colorado​, New Mexico and Utah.

item.description: Democratic state Rep. Gina Hinojosa, the Democrat running for governor in Texas, said there's "deep disappointment in both political parties" in the Lone Star State.

item.title: 10/25: Face The Nation
item.description: This week on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan," with the midterm elections less than 10 days away, CBS News executive director of elections and surveys Anthony Salvanto dives into our latest polling. Plus. retiring GOP Sen. Thom Tillis joins.

item.title: Venezuela opposition leader María Corina Machado returns to country
item.description: Machado covertly snuck out of the South American country in December with a private U.S. rescue team to accept the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize in Norway.

item.title: Blanche says DOJ is "doing our own research" with Alaska challenge
item.description: The Justice Department filed a lawsuit last week to preemptively challenge the certification of Alaska's Senate race if the Republican incumbent, Sen. Dan Sullivan, loses.

item.title: Alaska Senate candidate sustains "minor injuries" in car accident
item.description: Alaska Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola sustained "minor injuries" in a car accident, her campaign said.

item.title: Frances Haugen: The Facebook Whistleblower | 60 Minutes Archive
item.description: In 2021, Frances Haugen, a former Facebook employee turned whistleblower, told 60 Minutes that in her time with the company she saw "conflicts of interest between what was good for the public and what was good for Facebook."

item.title: GOP Sen. Tillis says "guardrails and accountability" needed after Starlink Ukraine slowdown
item.description: After Elon Musk's SpaceX temporarily throttled Starlink satellite communication system in Ukraine, Sen. Thom Tillis joined the growing number of Republican lawmakers speaking out against it. "I get it's a private company, but they're playing into military space, geopolitical space," Tillis said on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan. "There's got to be some guardrails and accountability, in my opinion."

item.title: Israeli election to test Netanyahu's ability to hold power
item.description: On Tuesday, Israel will hold its first parliamentary elections since the Oct. 7, 2023, terror attacks. Essentially one man is on the ballot: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. How might Israeli policy change if the opposition succeeds?

item.title: 100 years later, the mystery of Houdini's death endures
item.description: Harry Houdini, the greatest escape artist who ever lived, died 100 years ago on Halloween – a fact that has only burnished his image as a daredevil who often cheated death. But was there a cover-up involving the circumstances of his death?
